fact: Senegal's justice ministry officially launched the e-Justice platform on 2026-09-10 at the Lat Dior courthouse in Dakar, described as the business base for dematerialising penal, civil, commercial and social case chains for magistrates and clerks, with presidents of courts credited for piloting and testing it.

Le Soleil reported that e-Justice, carried by the Direction de la Dematerialisation et de l'Automatisation numerique with UNDP support, is to bring case enrolment, the general roll, Parquet and Greffe activity, instruction and appeals into one digital environment, with the Pikine-Guediawaye court among the pilot courts and an official launch set for 2026-09-10.

Ecofin reported that the Pikine-Guediawaye courthouse is a pilot site for the e-Justice programme supported by UNDP, with a roadmap developed for possible expansion and no extension to other courts announced.
Ecofin reported that the programme's final report records an e-Justice platform deployed in one court and five judicial procedures digitised.

The UN information centre in Dakar reported that the Pikine-Guediawaye court already had the e-justice pilot system on its own computers, to be fully operational in September 2025, with extension to Dakar courts planned from October 2025 and a nationwide roadmap, depending on funding.

Leral reported that the Pikine-Guediawaye court is piloting, with UNDP support, digitisation of judicial archives for later integration into the E-Justice platform, with first results judged satisfactory by the justice ministry on 2026-10-09 and extension to other courts possible.
